hypotheses.justification: Recover it as `(norm_nonneg (g.coeff 0 - f.coeff 0)).trans_lt (hcoeff 0)`, then use the existing proof unchanged. Thus ε ≤ 0 is already excluded by hcoeff, including for constant polynomials.

In Approximation.lean, the proof of the root-continuity estimate uses f.Monic only to establish f.natDegree ≠ 0 when f has the selected root. Replace that step using Polynomial.natDegree_pos_of_aeval_root, hfsep.ne_zero, the root equation, and injectivity of the field algebra map. Every other step of that estimate, its extension-field version, and the remaining Krasner argument is unchanged. Nonzero constants have no roots, so their case is vacuous. This deletion retains hdeg; hfm and hdeg cannot generally both be deleted.

Split on ε ≤ 1. In that case, unequal degrees contradict hcoeff at the larger degree: Polynomial.Monic.coeff_natDegree and Polynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt make the coefficient-difference norm equal to 1. Recover hdeg and use the existing proof. If ε > 1, Real.one_le_rpow shows the displayed radius is at least ‖x‖, even when the inverse exponent is zero. Thus hbound implies the Krasner inequality with y = 0. As in the existing rootwise argument, hfsep and hfsplit supply separability and splitting of minpoly K₀ x. IsKrasner.krasner then puts every reference root in K₀⟮0⟯ = ⊥, proving the inclusion regardless of g. Empty root sets are vacuous. This deletion retains hfm; the two cannot generally both be deleted.
